column1: # Metals on the strong edge sites of clays (2SPNE SC/CE, Bradbury and Baeyens), 25 C, zero ionic strength:
#   SsOH + Me+2 + y H2O = SsOMe(OH)y^(1-y) + (y+1) H+      log_k
# Rows with a log_k were fitted to measured sorption edges.  The other metals get theirs from the linear free
# energy relationship (LFER) between a surface constant and the metal's aqueous hydrolysis constant,
#   log SK(x-1) = a + b log OHK(x),   Me+2 + x H2O = Me(OH)x^(2-x) + x H+  (log OHK(x))
# with a = 7.9, b = 0.83 for illite (Bradbury and Baeyens 2009b, GCA 73, 1004-1013, eq. 9) and a = 8.1,
# b = 0.90 for montmorillonite (Bradbury and Baeyens 2005, GCA 69, 875-892, quoted as eq. 8 in 2009b).
# The hydrolysis constants (kind "hydrolysis", x in the y column) for Ni and Co are the ones Bradbury and
# Baeyens used (2009b Table 6: NEA 2005 for Ni, Baes and Mesmer 1976 for Co); for the other metals they are this
# calculator's own (OBIGT, SLOP98 and later, at 25 C and 1 bar), so the surface and aqueous chemistry agree.
# Rows of kind "lfer" carry a in the y column and b in the log_k column.
# Measured: Ni and Co on illite, Bradbury and Baeyens (2009a) GCA 73, 990-1003, Table 11.
